subject.title: refactor(memory): move QMD coordination to SQLite

question: Should the first release of SQLite QMD leases enforce coordination with still-running pre-upgrade processes, or is a documentation-only full-restart boundary acceptable?
rationale: Removing the shipped file locks while requiring operator restart is an upgrade and availability policy choice; code review cannot decide whether OpenClaw may intentionally leave mixed-version writers uncoordinated.

options.title: Enforce a transition boundary
options.body: Preserve legacy lock coordination for a bounded tagged transition or fail closed when an old-process owner may still be active, with an upgrade regression test.

options.title: Accept the hard restart cutover
options.body: Keep the no-dual-lock implementation but explicitly accept that QMD is unsafe until every process sharing the state directory has restarted.

options.title: Split the lease groundwork
options.body: Land the generic lease API and schema separately, then defer the QMD cutover until its upgrade boundary and live proof are settled.

recommendation.title: Enforce a transition boundary
recommendation.body: Preserve legacy lock coordination for a bounded tagged transition or fail closed when an old-process owner may still be active, with an upgrade regression test.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the existing QMD coordination fix and is the strongest available routing candidate for the upgrade-boundary decision.
